raw_response: Banks reported that the fourth quarter of 2023 included a large FDIC special assessment charge, which caused reported expenses to decrease year-over-year when compared to subsequent periods. For example, one bank noted that excluding this notable item, expenses were up 1% in Q4 2024 due to higher investments and merit increases, while another stated that reported expenses of $16 billion included the assessment, but excluding it, expenses increased by 10%. In early 2024, one bank noted a roughly $300 million release of prior period accruals for the FDIC special assessment, which partially offset expense increases. Another bank indicated that its full-year 2024 non-interest expense guidance was unchanged despite including the impact of the FDIC special assessment in the first quarter.
